17 EXAM FACTS — ACCOUNTING STANDARDS (Module 9)

① GAAP is the umbrella of rules/standards/procedures accountants must follow; Accounting Standards are the written policy documents issued within that framework.

② In India: ICAI's ASB issues AS for non-corporate entities/SMEs; the MCA notifies AS for corporate entities (based on ICAI's recommendations) via the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules.

③ Convergence (harmonising local GAAP with IFRS over time) ≠ Adoption (using IFRS exactly as issued). Ind AS is notified under Section 133, Companies Act 2013.

④ Ind AS Phase-I (companies): mandatory 1.4.2016 for net worth ≥ ₹500 cr. Phase-II: 1.4.2017 for net worth ₹250–<500 cr. Once opted in, a company must keep following Ind AS even if it later falls below the threshold.

⑤ AS 1's three fundamental accounting assumptions: Going Concern, Consistency, Accrual — disclose ONLY if NOT followed. Selection criteria: Prudence, Substance over Form, Materiality.

⑥ AS 1: disclosure of a policy or its change can NEVER remedy a wrong or inappropriate accounting treatment.

⑦ AS 10: PPE cost = purchase price (less trade discounts) + directly attributable costs to bring it to intended use + initial decommissioning/restoration estimate. Revaluation increase → credited to Revaluation Surplus, NEVER adjusted through accumulated depreciation.

⑧ Ind AS 16 REQUIRES the components approach; AS 10 does not. Ind AS 16 requires choosing Cost or Revaluation model; AS 10 merely "recognises" revaluation.

⑨ AS 11: Monetary items → revalued at CLOSING rate every balance sheet date, gain/loss to P&L. Non-monetary items at historical cost → NO revaluation at all. Exception: forex loss on a loan raised SPECIFICALLY for a fixed asset is added to that asset's carrying amount.

⑩ AS 11: Integral foreign operation → exchange difference to P&L. Non-integral → Balance Sheet items at closing rate, difference parked in Foreign Currency Translation Reserve until disposal.

⑪ Ind AS 21 uses the functional-currency approach and excludes forward contracts; AS 11 uses the integral/non-integral approach and includes forward contracts.

⑫ AS 12: Capital approach (promoters'-contribution grants → Capital Reserve) vs. Income approach (other grants → matched to related costs over time, never on a receipts basis). A depreciable-asset grant is deferred income spread with depreciation — never recognised in P&L all at once.

⑬ Ind AS 20 requires non-monetary grants at FAIR VALUE and bars crediting grants directly to shareholders' funds; AS 12 uses acquisition cost/nominal value and specifically allows a capital-reserve treatment for non-depreciable-asset grants.

⑭ AS 16: only a QUALIFYING ASSET (substantial time to get ready for use/sale) attracts capitalised borrowing cost; capitalisation follows the ASSET, not the whole loan — advances, working capital, and ready-to-use assets funded from the same loan are always expensed.

⑮ AS 16: general-borrowing capitalisation rate = weighted average cost of outstanding borrowings EXCLUDING asset-specific borrowings; capitalisation suspends during interruption of active development but NOT during a normal, necessary temporary delay (e.g. seasonal monsoon).

⑯ AS 22: only TIMING differences (capable of reversal) create a DTA/DTL; PERMANENT differences (e.g. tax penalty) create NEITHER. DTA on unabsorbed depreciation/losses needs VIRTUAL certainty with convincing evidence; other DTAs need only REASONABLE certainty. Deferred tax is NEVER discounted.

⑰ Ind AS 12 uses the Balance Sheet approach (carrying amount vs. tax base; taxable/deductible temporary differences, no Permanent Differences concept); AS 22 uses the Income Statement approach (taxable vs. accounting income; Timing vs. Permanent Differences) and alone gives specific guidance on MAT u/s 115JB and tax holidays.

MODULE 9 CLOSING DRILL (retrieval practice — do not skip): put this document down and, on rough paper, write from memory: the difference between Convergence and Adoption; the Ind AS net-worth thresholds for Phase-I and Phase-II companies; AS 1's three fundamental assumptions and its three policy-selection criteria; the AS 10 elements of cost and the Cost-vs-Revaluation-model treatment; the AS 11 rule for monetary items and its one named exception; the Integral vs. Non-integral translation rules; the AS 12 Capital-vs-Income approach and the two presentation methods for asset-linked grants; the AS 16 test for a Qualifying Asset and the capitalisation-rate formula; and the AS 22 Timing-vs-Permanent difference distinction with the reasonable-vs-virtual certainty test for DTA recognition. For each of the six standards, also try to name ONE point on which its Ind AS counterpart differs. Check against the notes only after finishing — answering from memory is what converts today's reading into exam-day marks. Anything you could not retrieve, star it and re-attempt tomorrow morning. Estimated time: twelve minutes.
The Final Ladder — Every Formula, Format and Rule in Paper 6

One climb through all nine modules, formulas and formats only. Read this straight through the morning of the exam — not to learn anything new, only to fire the recall pathway for what you already know.

Section A · Accounting Fundamentals (15%)

ModuleThe Ladder
1. Accounting FundamentalsFour Frameworks: Conceptual (fills gaps when no standard applies) · Legal (Companies Act 2013, Partnership Act 1932, LLP Act 2008, etc.) · Institutional (ICAI's AS/Ind AS + ICMAI's 24 CAS) · Regulatory (RBI/SEBI/IRDAI/PFRDA/TRAI layered on top — never confuse with Institutional) · 9 Concepts: Entity, Going Concern, Accounting Period, Money Measurement, Accrual, Dual Aspect, Matching, Realisation, Cost · 4 Conventions: Conservatism, Consistency, Materiality, Full Disclosure · Assets = Liabilities + Capital · AS-26 bars Deferred Revenue Expenditure for advertising/R&D/training — expensed now · Capital Exp. before OR after commencement; Revenue Exp. always after · COA number ranges 1000–8999 (Assets·Liabilities·Equity·Revenue·COGS·Expenses·Other Rev.·Other Exp.) · Special Journals = credit + GOODS only; cash goes to Cash Book, non-goods credit to Journal Proper · Ledger: Personal (Debtors/Creditors) vs Impersonal (Real+Nominal) · Cash Book: Single/Double/Triple(+Discount)/Multi-columnar; Contra Entry "C" both sides · BRS reconciles Cash Book bank column vs Pass Book, never rectifies an error itself · SLM Dep. = (V−S)÷n; WDV Dep. = Opening WDV × Rate · A tallied Trial Balance is only prima facie evidence of accuracy — Omission/Commission/Principle/Original Entry/Compensating errors all survive it.

Section B · Accounting for Special Transactions (10%)

Sub-topicThe Ladder
2.1 Bills of ExchangeS.5 NI Act 1881: unconditional order in writing, signed by maker, certain sum, certain person · 3 Days of Grace for After Date/After Sight bills, none for Demand/At Sight bills · national holiday on due date → shift 1 day EARLIER; emergency holiday → shift 1 day LATER (grace added first, either way) · Bills Receivable = drawer's asset; Bills Payable = drawee's liability · Discount (drawer's expense, from date of bank-discounting) vs Rebate (holder's expense/drawee's income, from date of retirement) — same formula, opposite direction and opposite party · dishonour by non-acceptance = no entries; by non-payment = entries in drawer/drawee/endorsee books · noting charges always ultimately recoverable from the dishonouring acceptor, whoever pays the notary first · Renewal = old bill cancelled + fresh bill + interest for the extension.
2.2–2.3 Consignment & Joint VentureConsignee passes NO entry on mere receipt of goods; ownership stays with consignor until actual sale · Ordinary and Del Credere Commission both on GROSS (total) sales unless the question restricts it; del credere PROVIDED → bad debts hit the consignee's own Commission A/c, NOT provided → they hit Consignment A/c · non-recurring "getting there" expenses (freight, transit insurance, clearing, customs) enter stock/goods-in-transit/abnormal-loss valuation; recurring expenses (godown rent, selling exp., commission) never do · Normal loss deducted before Abnormal loss ONLY when both occur at the SAME point; an in-transit abnormal loss is valued off the original despatch quantity, before any normal loss · Stock at Invoice Price still carries the Load — cancelled via Stock Reserve = Load × (Unsold ÷ Total sent) · Joint Venture = temporary partnership, no firm name, profit shared EQUALLY absent agreement (the partnership default) · Joint Venture A/c is debited with EVERY expense (capital or revenue, personal or common); stock/asset taken over by a co-venturer is credited to JV A/c and debited to him, exactly like a sale.

Section C · Preparation of Financial Statements (20%)

Sub-topicThe Ladder
3.1 Commercial OrganisationsTrading A/c: Opening Stock + Purchases (net) + Direct Exp. vs. Sales (net) + Closing Stock → Gross Profit/Loss · P&L A/c: indirect Admin/Selling/Distribution exp. & abnormal losses vs. revenue/other income → Net Profit/Loss · P&L Appropriation A/c (partnership firms only): Interest on Capital, Partners' Salary/Commission, Reserve, Divisible Profit · Manufacturing A/c (manufacturers only) precedes Trading A/c · Balance Sheet marshalling: Rigidity/Permanence order (most permanent first) vs. Liquidity order (most liquid first) · "Wages & Salaries" (first word Wages → Trading A/c) vs. "Salaries & wages" (first word Salaries → P&L A/c); Carriage Inward (Trading A/c) vs. Carriage Outward (P&L A/c) · Single-vs-Double Rule: a Trial-Balance item posts ONCE; an outside-TB adjustment always posts TWICE, in two different statements.
3.2 Not-for-Profit OrganisationsReceipts & Payments A/c = summarised Cash Book, cash basis, ANY period, capital+revenue, Real A/c · Income & Expenditure A/c = accrual basis, CURRENT period only, revenue items only, Nominal A/c, balance = Surplus/Deficit → Capital/Accumulated Fund · Subscription for the year = Cash received + Closing O/s − Opening O/s + Opening Advance − Closing Advance (all four legs, every time) · earmarked donations (e.g. Building Fund) and income on fund investments stay INSIDE the Special Fund (a Balance Sheet liability), never crossing Income & Expenditure A/c · Entrance fees: no universal rule — follow the institution's by-laws or the question's stated instruction (capitalised, split, or fully revenue — all three appear) · a trading activity (Restaurant/Bar) contributes only its NET trading profit to the I&E A/c, as one line.
3.3 Incomplete RecordsStatement of Affairs (not a Balance Sheet) gives Opening & Closing Capital as balancing figures · Profit = (Closing Capital − Opening Capital) + Drawings (ADD back) − Additional Capital Introduced (DEDUCT) · then less further adjustments (int. on capital/drawings, depreciation, bad debts) → Net Profit → less appropriations → Divisible Profit · a Total Debtors/Creditors A/c's balancing-figure identity changes case to case — check what's already GIVEN before assuming what's missing · cash defalcation by an employee is carried to the Balance Sheet as a recoverable ASSET ("Amount Recoverable from Cashier"), not written off straight to P&L.

Section D · Partnership Accounting (20%)

Sub-topicThe Ladder
4.1–4.2 AdmissionSacrificing Ratio = Old Ratio − New Ratio (old partners only); goodwill premium shared strictly in THIS ratio · Goodwill: (1) Avg. Profits × Years' Purchase; (2) Super Profit (=Future Maintainable Profit − Normal Return on Capital Employed) × Years' Purchase; (3) Capitalisation of (Super) Profits = (Profit÷Normal Rate of Return)×100 [− Actual Capital Employed]; (4) Annuity Method = Super Profit × PV Annuity Factor · ordinary Revaluation A/c → OLD partners, OLD ratio only; Memorandum Revaluation → 1st half OLD ratio, 2nd (reversal) half NEW ratio incl. new partner · partial cash goodwill: FULL premium still credited to old partners in sacrificing ratio; shortfall debited to the new partner's own Capital/Current A/c · a partner's Current A/c can sit on EITHER side — total each individually, never assume credit.
4.3 RetirementGaining Ratio = New Ratio − Old Ratio (continuing partners); Gaining Partners' Capital A/c Dr. → To Outgoing Partner's Capital A/c, in Gaining Ratio · Revaluation, Reserves & accumulated profits → ALL partners, OLD ratio · S.37 Indian Partnership Act, 1932: delayed settlement → retiring partner gets the HIGHER of (a) profit share on present adjusted capitals, or (b) 6% p.a. interest on the amount due.
4.4 Death of a Partner & Joint Life PolicyIdentical to retirement (Old ratio for splits, Gaining ratio for goodwill compensation) + interim profit share estimated on Time Basis (avg. profit × elapsed-time ratio) or Sales Basis (last year's Profit÷Sales rate × actual interim sales) + settlement to the EXECUTOR, with interest on any unpaid balance from date of death to date of payment · JLP Method A (not an asset): premium = pure P&L expense · JLP Method B (asset at surrender value): Approach 1 (single a/c, excess premium over SV-rise written to P&L) vs. Approach 2 (JLP Reserve A/c, funded via P&L Appropriation) — the Reserve is NOT distributable profit, and closes into JLP A/c before profit-on-maturity is struck · over-stated book goodwill's excess slice is written off in the OLD ratio (incl. the deceased); only the correctly-valued remainder is written off among continuing partners.
4.5 Dissolution & InsolvencyS.48(1): losses → Profits → Capital → Partners individually (PSR) · S.48(2) asset order: (i) third-party debts → (ii) Partners' Loan (ranks AHEAD of any partner's capital) → (iii) Partners' Capital → (iv) residue in PSR · an insolvent partner's deficiency (Garner v. Murray / S.48(b)(ii)) is shared by SOLVENT partners in their LAST AGREED CAPITAL ratio, never PSR · unrecorded assets/liabilities must be brought into Realisation A/c, never skipped · piecemeal distribution: Maximum Loss = Total Due to Partners − Cash Available, re-computed FRESH at EVERY instalment — OR the Highest Relative (Surplus) Capital Method, paid strictly by rank, converging to PSR only at the very end.
4.6–4.8 Amalgamation, Conversion & LLPNet Assets Acquired vs. Purchase Consideration: equal → no Goodwill/Capital Reserve; PC higher → Goodwill (debit, balancing); PC lower → Capital Reserve (credit, balancing) · goodwill-on-amalgamation is a TERM OF THE SCHEME — sometimes raised, sometimes explicitly ignored; read the scheme · a partner's credit balance above his agreed fixed capital is settled in CASH only if available, else becomes a LOAN to the new entity · the share component of PC is a BALANCING figure, never assumed at face value — can throw up Securities Premium · LLP formats keep "Contribution Received" (Partners' Funds) separate from "Reserves and Surplus" (absorbs the year's P&L); no statutory Trading/P&L A/c + Balance Sheet — runs off Form 8's two prescribed statements.

Section E · Lease, Branch and Departmental Accounts etc. (15%, shared across Modules 5–8)

ModuleThe Ladder
5. Lease Accounting (AS 19)Finance Lease if ANY ONE of 5 situations applies (title transfer · bargain purchase option · lease term = major part of economic life · PV of Minimum Lease Payments ≈ substantially all fair value · specialised asset) — not all five together, and not by title alone · lessee recognises BOTH the leased asset AND a liability, at the LOWER of fair value or PV of MLP · finance charge = constant RATE applied to the OUTSTANDING (reducing) liability every year, never the original principal · reclassification only on mutual agreement to change lease PROVISIONS (not renewal); mere changes in estimates/circumstances never reclassify · Sale-and-Leaseback: Finance-lease leaseback → profit/loss ALWAYS deferred, amortised with depreciation; Operating-lease leaseback → runs on the fair-value test (at/above = immediate; below, unless compensated by future below-market rentals = deferred).
6.1 Branch AccountsDebtors System / Stock & Debtors System / Final Accounts Method for DEPENDENT branches only · bad debts, discount allowed and sales returns never appear separately in the Branch A/c — the closing Debtors figure is already net of them · an independent (or foreign) branch keeps its OWN full books and Trial Balance, incorporated ONCE at year-end via the H.O. Account — never Debtors-Method micro-entries · foreign branch TB translation: Opening Stock @ opening rate; revenue items (Sales/Salaries/Rent) @ average rate; monetary items (Cash/Bank/Debtors/Expenses O/s) @ closing rate; Fixed Assets @ historical rate on acquisition; H.O. A/c @ the figure already recorded in H.O.'s own books; balancing "Difference in Exchange" to the Branch P&L A/c.
6.2 Departmental AccountsApportionment driver by nature: Rent/Rates/Insurance/Heating → FLOOR AREA; Wages/Welfare → NUMBER OF EMPLOYEES; Carriage Inwards/Purchase Commission → PURCHASES; Selling Exp./Discount Allowed/Bad Debts → SALES — swapping the basis silently misallocates profit while the overall total still tallies · unrealised profit in closing stock is valued at the TRANSFEROR (sending) department's GP rate, never the holding department's own rate · Provision for Unrealised Profit is reversed on OPENING stock too (last year's rate), net-charged to General P&L A/c, for EVERY predecessor department in a transfer chain · a stated minimum guaranteed managerial commission is payable even on a loss-making department; recompute commission only AFTER removing unrealised profit.
7. Insurance Claim for Loss of Stock & Loss of ProfitLoss of Stock: Memorandum Trading A/c (last year's GP rate × this period's Sales) → Closing Stock as the balancing figure = estimated stock at the date of fire · Net Claim = Actual Loss × (Sum Insured ÷ Stock Value at date of fire); Average Clause bites only when Sum Insured < Stock Value (genuine under-insurance) · abnormal/defective items are stripped OUT of Opening Stock/Purchases/Sales FIRST to find the true "normal" GP rate · a paid claim (no additional premium) REDUCES the sum insured available for a later loss in the same period · Loss of Profit: GP = Net Profit + Insured Standing Charges (or, on a loss, Insured Standing Charges − proportionate Net Loss); Short Sales = Standard Turnover − Actual Turnover; Gross Claim = GP Lost + Admissible Additional Expenses (least of 3 tests) − savings, with the Average Clause applied ONCE to the combined Gross Claim; the trend adjustment applies to Standard Turnover and Insurable-Value turnover, never to Actual turnover.
8. Hire Purchase & Instalment SaleOwnership passes on the LAST instalment (Hire Purchase) vs. IMMEDIATELY at the agreement (Instalment Sale) — the only true test, not the mere fact of staggered payment · HP Price = Cash Price + Total Interest · 4 interest-apportionment Situations (I: rate+CP+instalments given, direct; II: rate+instalments given, CP missing, peel backward; III: only instalments given, equal cash-price share, simultaneous equations; IV: rate+equal instalments+annuity factor, CP missing) plus Ratio-of-Outstanding-Balances (unequal instalments) / Sum-of-the-Years-Digits (equal instalments) when only Total Interest is known · a repossessed asset is recorded at its AGREED/REVALUED value, never book value; on partial repossession the Vendor's A/c closes only by the AGREED value of goods actually surrendered.

Section F · Accounting Standards (20%)

Sub-topicThe Ladder
9.1 GAAP, AS & Convergence to Ind ASGAAP = the profession's own rules/conventions/standards for uniform record-keeping · Accounting Standards = written policy documents by a recognised expert body (ICAI) covering recognition/measurement/presentation/disclosure · Convergence ≠ Adoption: Ind AS are India's OWN standards, formulated for the Indian environment, aimed at converging WITH (not literally adopting) IFRS as issued by the IFRS Foundation · applicability phased by net-worth thresholds under the Ind AS roadmap.
AS 1 & AS 10AS 1 (Disclosure of Accounting Policies): all significant policies disclosed at ONE place; disclosure NEVER cures a wrong treatment; a material current-period policy change → disclose the change AND the amount (or state if not ascertainable); no material effect now but expected later → disclose in the period adopted · AS 10 (Property, Plant and Equipment): measured at COST on recognition [(a) purchase price net of discounts (b) directly attributable costs (c) decommissioning/restoration estimate]; post-recognition, choose Cost Model OR Revaluation Model for a whole asset class — a revaluation increase credits Revaluation Surplus (unless reversing a prior P&L decrease); a decrease charges P&L (unless offsetting an existing Revaluation Surplus).
AS 11 & AS 12AS 11 (Forex): Monetary items → CLOSING rate every balance sheet date, difference to P&L; Non-monetary at historical cost → NEVER revalued; Non-monetary at fair value → rate ruling when fair value was determined; ONE exception — exchange difference on repaying a liability incurred SPECIFICALLY to acquire a fixed asset adjusts that asset's carrying amount · AS 12 (Government Grants): grant for a SPECIFIC fixed asset → deduct from the asset's gross value (reduced depreciation) OR treat as deferred income spread over useful life (non-depreciable-asset grants → Capital Reserve); revenue grants → credit P&L / deduct from the related expense; PROMOTERS'-CONTRIBUTION-type grants (tied to total investment, no repayment expected) → Capital Reserve, regardless of that year's results.
AS 16 & AS 22AS 16 (Borrowing Costs): only borrowing cost directly attributable to a QUALIFYING ASSET is capitalised — follows the ASSET, not the loan; Specific borrowing → actual cost incurred less income on temporary investment; General borrowing → Capitalisation Rate (weighted average of borrowings, excluding specific ones) × expenditure on the asset; capitalised cost per period never exceeds actual borrowing cost incurred · AS 22 (Taxes on Income): only TIMING differences (capable of reversing later, e.g. unabsorbed depreciation) create DTA/DTL; PERMANENT differences (e.g. a tax penalty) create NEITHER; DTA recognition subject to PRUDENCE (VIRTUAL certainty needed where unabsorbed depreciation/carried-forward losses exist); DTA/DTL are never discounted to present value.
The Master Trap List — The Distractors This Paper Is Built From

Every numerical slip and every half-remembered format traces back to one of these confusions. Read once, slowly, the morning of the exam.

1. The Institutional Framework is the standard-setters (ICAI's AS/Ind AS, ICMAI's CAS), not the sector regulators — RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA and TRAI belong to the separate, fourth pillar: the Regulatory Framework.

2. The 9-vs-4 split of Concepts and Conventions is fixed — Concepts are foundational assumptions that don't change (Entity, Going Concern, Accounting Period, Money Measurement, Accrual, Dual Aspect, Matching, Realisation, Cost); Conventions are customary practices that can shift over time (Conservatism, Consistency, Materiality, Full Disclosure).

3. AS-26 killed Deferred Revenue Expenditure treatment for advertising, R&D, training and promotional spend — all of it is a straight revenue expense of the period incurred, never carried forward as an asset.

4. The Purchase and Sales Day Books record CREDIT transactions in GOODS only — cash purchases/sales of goods go to the Cash Book, and a credit purchase/sale of any non-goods asset goes to the Journal Proper, regardless of how routine the item looks.

5. A tallied Trial Balance is only prima facie evidence of arithmetical accuracy — Errors of Omission, Commission, Principle, Original Entry and Compensating Errors all leave it perfectly balanced.

6. A pre-known national holiday on a bill's due date shifts it one day EARLIER; an emergency (unforeseen) holiday shifts it one day LATER — and the 3 Days of Grace are always added first, before either holiday check.

7. Discount and Rebate share the same formula but run in opposite directions — Discount is the drawer's expense from the date of bank-discounting; Rebate is the holder's expense (drawee's income) from the date of early retirement, computed only on the genuinely unexpired period.

8. Del credere commission is calculated on TOTAL (cash + credit) sales unless the question explicitly restricts it to credit sales — the commission exists to guarantee collection risk, but its base is gross sales by default.

9. The consignee passes no entry merely on receiving consigned goods, and bad debts follow whoever guaranteed collection — charged to the consignee's own Commission A/c when del credere is paid, to Consignment A/c when it is not.

10. Normal loss is deducted before abnormal loss only when both occur at the same point — an abnormal loss occurring in transit is valued straight off the originally despatched quantity, before any later-discovered normal loss is even applied.

11. Stock or an asset taken over by a co-venturer is credited to Joint Venture A/c and debited to that co-venturer, exactly like a sale — and every venture expense, personal or through the Joint Bank, is debited to Joint Venture A/c without exception.

12. Read the first word of a Trial Balance label — "Wages & Salaries" goes to the Trading Account, "Salaries & wages" goes to the Profit & Loss Account, and by the same logic Carriage Inwards (bringing goods IN) is direct while Carriage Outwards is an indirect, selling-side expense.

13. Subscription needs all four legs, not two — Cash received + Closing Outstanding − Opening Outstanding + Opening Advance − Closing Advance, every single time.

14. Earmarked donations and any income on a Special Fund's investments stay inside that fund as a Balance Sheet liability — they never cross the Income & Expenditure Account.

15. Entrance fees have no single universal rule — fully capitalised, part-capitalised, or fully revenue all appear across different questions; follow the institution's by-laws or the question's own stated instruction.

16. Drawings are ADDED BACK and Additional Capital Introduced is DEDUCTED when reconstructing profit from a change in capital — flipping either sign is the single most common Incomplete Records error.

17. Sacrificing Ratio is Old Ratio minus New Ratio, for old partners only — the goodwill premium a new partner brings in is shared strictly in this ratio, never in the old ratio or the new ratio alone.

18. An ordinary Revaluation Account always distributes in the OLD ratio; only a Memorandum Revaluation Account flips its second half to the NEW ratio, including the incoming partner.

19. Gaining Ratio (New minus Old) belongs to retirement and death; Sacrificing Ratio (Old minus New) belongs to admission — using the wrong formula flips who compensates whom.

20. A deceased or retiring partner's interim profit share follows either the Time Basis (average profit spread evenly by elapsed months) or the Sales Basis (last year's Profit÷Sales rate applied to actual interim sales) — the question's own wording decides which.

21. Interest runs on an executor's unpaid balance from the date of death to the date of actual payment — simply transferring the deceased partner's closing capital balance and stopping there ignores this charge.

22. The same Joint Life Policy premium gets opposite treatment depending on the method — a pure Profit & Loss expense under Method A, a capitalised asset under Method B; and a JLP Reserve is never distributable profit, closing into JLP A/c before any profit-on-maturity is struck.

23. Section 48(2) ranks a Partners' Loan strictly ahead of any partner's Capital on dissolution — distributing to capital before clearing a partner's loan is a common ordering error.

24. An insolvent partner's deficiency is shared by the solvent partners in their LAST AGREED CAPITAL ratio (Garner v. Murray), never in the profit-sharing ratio.

25. The "maximum possible loss" assumption in piecemeal distribution must be recomputed fresh at every single instalment — treating one round's figure as final understates what later partners are actually owed.

26. The share component of a Purchase Consideration is always a balancing figure, never assumed at face value — it can silently generate a Securities Premium for the acquiring company.

27. A lease is a Finance Lease if ANY ONE of AS 19's five tests is satisfied — demanding all five together, or judging purely by whether title transfers, both understate how often a lease is really a finance lease.

28. The finance charge on a lease liability is a constant RATE applied to the outstanding (reducing) balance every year, never to the original principal — the rate stays fixed even as the rupee charge keeps falling.

29. Bad debts, discount allowed and sales returns never appear as separate lines inside a Branch Account — the closing Debtors figure given in the question is already net of them.

30. An independent or foreign branch keeps its own complete set of books, incorporated into Head Office accounts only ONCE at year-end — applying Debtors-System micro-entries to it either double-records transactions or never reconciles.

31. Every departmental apportionment item has its own natural driver — Rent/Rates/Insurance on floor area, Wages on headcount, Carriage Inwards on Purchases, Selling Expenses on Sales — swapping the basis silently misallocates profit while the grand total still tallies.

32. Unrealised profit sitting in one department's closing stock is valued at the TRANSFEROR department's own Gross Profit rate, never the rate of the department currently holding the stock.

33. Abnormal, defective or heavily-discounted items must be stripped out of Opening Stock, Purchases and Sales before computing the "normal" Gross Profit rate for an insurance stock claim — leaving them in distorts the whole estimate.

34. The Average Clause bites only when the Sum Insured is strictly LESS than the value of stock (or the Insurable Value) at the date of loss — adequate or over-insurance never triggers a proportionate reduction.

35. In a Loss-of-Profit claim, GP Lost and Admissible Additional Expenses are combined into one Gross Claim before the Average Clause ratio is applied ONCE — never applied separately to each component.

36. Staggered instalment payment alone never proves Hire Purchase — only WHEN ownership passes (on the last instalment, versus immediately at the agreement for an Instalment Sale) tells the two arrangements apart, along with every downstream default and repossession right.

37. Choosing the wrong one of the six interest-apportionment methods is the most common Hire Purchase error — read exactly what the question gives (rate, cash price, equal or unequal instalments, an annuity factor) before picking Situation I–IV, Ratio of Outstanding Balances, or Sum-of-the-Years-Digits.

38. A repossessed asset is recorded at its AGREED (revalued) value, never at its book value — and on partial repossession the Vendor's Account is closed only by the agreed value of the goods actually surrendered, not the full outstanding balance.

39. Convergence with IFRS is not Adoption of IFRS — Ind AS remain India's own standards, formulated for the Indian environment and aimed only at converging with the IFRS Foundation's standards.

40. Disclosing an accounting policy in the notes never cures a wrong treatment applied in the accounts (AS 1) — disclosure and correctness are two separate requirements.

41. Monetary items revalue at closing rate to Profit & Loss, with one AS 11 exception — exchange differences on repaying a liability incurred specifically to acquire a fixed asset are adjusted into that asset's own carrying amount instead.

42. A government grant's Capital-vs-Revenue treatment depends on the condition attached to it, not merely on whether it relates to "setting up" or "acquiring an asset."

43. AS 16 capitalisation follows the ASSET, not the loan — only the interest attributable to actual qualifying-asset expenditure is capitalised; the rest of the same loan's interest is expensed regardless of the loan's stated purpose.

44. Only TIMING differences create deferred tax; PERMANENT differences (like a tax penalty) create neither a Deferred Tax Asset nor a Deferred Tax Liability.

In the hallSkim the full question paper first before committing to an order of attempt. Open every answer with the correct account/statement name (or the AS/Section number, where one applies) before the figures themselves — a correctly labelled proforma earns marks even if a later balancing figure goes wrong. Never abandon a partly-worked numerical question for a fresh one; a Trading Account, Branch Account or Realisation Account half-built in the right format is worth more than a blank page.

Weight-based priority if time runs out anywhere in this plan: Modules 3, 4 and 9 (20% each, 60% combined) are never the ones you cut. Module 1 (15%) is foundational groundwork that every other module's journal entries assume you already have. Modules 5–8 (15% combined) are four distinct topics sharing one weight-slot — a focused pass on just their classification tests and core formulas outperforms a diffuse re-read of all four. Module 2 (10%) is the smallest weight and, being format-driven rather than judgment-driven, the fastest to shore up if you're short on hours.

This page is exam strategy, not syllabus content — every fact it points to lives in the verified module pages above, condensed strictly from ICMAI's own Paper 6 Study Notes (Syllabus 2022).
